result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection on a wide, multi-lane arterial road with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and marked crosswalks. However, the environment is dominated by vehicle travel lanes, featuring long crossing distances and faded pavement markings that reduce pedestrian comfort and safety.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four travel lanes plus turn lanes without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground and center.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground pavement crossing the main road.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to high-speed travel lanes with no planting strip or parked cars to provide a physical or psychological buffer.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalks using high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide multi-lane arterial road with faded crossing markings and poor walkway continuity. result.summary: A quiet residential street featuring mature tree canopies and continuous sidewalks on both sides. The environment is generally pedestrian-friendly due to its narrow feel and low-speed design, though parked cars create significant visual obstructions for crossing.

hazards.name: Parked Car Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs in this mid-block section, which may lead to unpredictable crossing behavior.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire visible roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental style crosswalk markings at the nearest intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install vertical deflection measures to maintain low vehicle speeds in this residential environment.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses, mature trees, and parallel on-street parking. Pedestrians have a dedicated sidewalk, though its effective width is constrained by large tree trunks and proximity to parked vehicles.
